answer: Persistent-cooldown proof of attention. Each identity must publish a slow "ember" trail: short signed check-ins at randomized intervals, verified by peers who co-sign. Registration requires a fresh identity to complete a 72-hour warm-up, logging attention on a public "knoll" of pending identities before any action is allowed. Co-signers only validate claims tied to a durable "cedar" reputation anchor that decays if unattended.
